query:
Which supplied authorities help analyze the live Delhi DRC1958s14(1)(b) issue shown by this allowed record, respecting the target procedural stage, rival assertions and scope limits? Do not predict the withheld target verdict.
    JUDGEMENT:
1. The petitioner filed the present petition for eviction of the tenant/ respondent under cite8†section 14(1)(b) of DRC Act.
2. It is stated by the petitioner that respondent no.1 who is a tenant at premises No. A- 4, Gopal Nagar, Azadpur, Delhi as shown in red colour in the site plan. It is stated that the tenanted premises was let out by the petitioner to respondent No.1 for manufacturing bobbins as proprietor of M/s Mukesh Contd........
E.No. 385/06/04 2
Bobbin Product (India). It is stated that respondent no.1 has sublet the old tenanted premises to M/s Balaji Enterprises i.e. respondent no.2 in April, 2003 without obtaining the consent in writing from the petitioner. It is prayed that eviction order may kindly be passed against the respondent.
3. The notice of the petition was issued to the respondent. The respondent in written statement raised the preliminary objection that petitioner has concealed the material facts that the property had already been acquired by the Land Acquisition Collector, Narela and the petitioner is not the owner of the suit property. It is stated on behalf of the respondent that the tenancy is very old.
It is stated that the petitioner has caused substantial damages to the roof of the suit premises and on account of which water is leaking in the shop thereby damaging the goods and articles. It is stated that the answering respondent no.1 Sh. Surender Kumar and Sh. Chajju Ram, his father are joint tenants in the shop and the tenancy stands in the name of M/s Chajju Ram Surender Kumar which is clearly reflected from the recent receipt enclosed herewith.
It is stated that M/s Mukesh Bobbin Products (India) and M/s Balaji Enterprises are sole proprietorship concern of the respondent Contd........
E.No. 385/06/04 3
no.1 Surender Kumar. It is stated that the sole proprietorship concern has no legal identity and it cannot be sued in its own name. Hence, the petition is bad for mis joinder of necessary parties and non-joinder of Chajju Ram. It is stated that petitioner has intentionally and deliberately not disclosed the status of the Balaji Enterprises as the firm is owned by the answering respondent. The respondent on the reply on merit denied the submissions of the petitioner.
4. The petitioner filed the replication whereby reaffirmed and reassert the contents of the plaint. It is stated that Sh. Chajju Ram has never been tenant and never paid rent. It is stated that tenancy is in the name of Sh. Surender Kumar, Proprietor of M/s Mukesh Bobbin Products India and M/s Balaji Enterprises is an unauthorised sub-tenant.
5. The petitioner to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and deposed in terms of the petition. The petitioner has also proved the documents Ex. PW1/1 i.e. the site plan of the suit premises and document Ex. PW1/2 certified copy of the eviction petition E. No.360/04. During cross-examination it is admitted by the petitioner that he purchased the suit property in the year 1999 from Sh. Ved Prakash. PW-1 denied that the land is acquired Contd........
E.No. 385/06/04 4
by the Land Acquisition Collector, Narela. It is admitted that the respondent is proprietor of M/s Mukesh Bobbin Products, however, it is denied that respondent is also the proprietor of M/s Balaji Enterprises.
6. PW-2 Sh. Rakesh Bist, Clerk from Oriental Bank of Commerce, Azadpur, who proved the current account of M/s Mukesh Bobbins Product India at the tenanted premises 41-A, Gopal Nagar, Azadpur, Delhi showing Sh. Surender Kumar as proprietor, copy of the same is proved as Ex. PW2/1.
7. PW-3 Sh. Phool Singh, Inspector Sale Tax, produced the summoned record in respect of M/s Balaji Enterprises at the tenanted premises and copy of the same are proved as Ex. PW3/1 to Ex. PW3/6. During cross-examination PW-3 admitted that proprietor of M/s Mukesh Bobbins Products and M/s Balaji Enterprises is Sh. Surender Kumar.
8. The respondent examined himself as RW-1 and deposed in terms of the written statement. The respondent during his cross- examination admitted that the petitioner filed another petition under cite9†section 14(1)(a) of DRC Act, 1958 which was dismissed. During cross-examination it is denied that it was held that Sh. Naresh Kumar is landlord and Surender Kumar, Contd........
E.No. 385/06/04 5
proprietor of Mukesh Bobbins Products (India) is tenant. It is also admitted by the respondent that he sent the money order four days back which was refused. It is also admitted that at the time of purchase of the property in question by the petitioner he was running the factory in the name of Mukesh Bobbin products (India). It is also admitted that he was not running the factory in the name of Mukesh Bobbins Product (India) since, 2003.
It is denied that the respondent is running shop from the tenanted premises. It is admitted that presently the sales tax is deposited in the name of Balaji Enterprises. RW-1 denied the suggestion that he has no concern with the tenanted premises and that he is not its proprietor. It is also admitted that he has not filed any petition in any court till date to show that Surender Kumar Chajju Ram Proprietor of M/s Balaji Enterprises is the tenant.
10.It is submitted by the ld. Counsel for the petitioner that it is the admitted case of the respondent no.1 that tenancy was created in the name of Sh. Surender Kumar, proprietor of M/s Mukesh Bobbin Products (India) and the business is being done by the Contd........
E.No. 385/06/04 6
respondent no.2 i.e. Balaji Enterprises from the tenanted premises. Therefore, petition may kindly be allowed.
11.On the other hand it is submitted by the counsel for respondent that premises was let out to the respondent no.1 in his personal capacity and he was doing the work in the name of M/s Mukesh Bobbin Products (India) and now he has started doing the work in the tenanted premises with the name of Balaji Enterprises. It is stated that respondent no.1 is the proprietor of respondent no.2, therefore, there is no subletting or parting with the possession of the tenanted premises.
No new legal entity has been created, therefore, it is prayed that petition may kindly be dismissed. Counsel for respondent relied upon the following judgements:
> (1)All India R. C. J. 1970, Supreme Court page 922, (2) All India R. C. J. 1986, Supreme Court page 404, (3)1993 (2) RCR Delhi High Court page 653, (4) 1994 (2) RCR Delhi High Court, (5) 2000 (2) RCR, Delhi High Court page 532, (6) 2003 (2) RCR Punjab and Har. Page 302, (7) 2003(1) RCR Punjab and Har. Page 99, (8) 2005 (2) RCR Punjab and Har. Page 649.
